title: Floral Diversity & Microbiology
notes: **Binomial nomenclature** was introduced by Carolus Linnaeus — every organism gets two names: generic name + specific epithet (e.g. Mangifera indica).
**Five kingdom classification (Whittaker):** Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia — based on cell structure, body organisation and nutrition.

**Algae:** chlorophyll-bearing, aquatic thalloid organisms; green algae (Spirogyra) have ribbon-shaped spiral chloroplasts; brown algae (Laminaria) have fucoxanthin; red algae (Polysiphonia) contain r-phycoerythrin.
**Bryophytes:** amphibians of the plant kingdom; need water for fertilisation; e.g. mosses and liverworts.
**Bacteria:** prokaryotic, reproduce by binary fission; useful forms fix nitrogen (Rhizobium) and ferment milk into curd (Lactobacillus).
**Virus:** acellular obligate parasite with DNA or RNA core and protein coat (capsid); e.g. TMV, HIV.
**Fungi:** heterotrophic, cell wall of chitin; yeast is unicellular and used in fermentation; Penicillium gives the antibiotic penicillin.
